I make mine a bit differently. This recipe gives a general idea, but is lacking. Here are some tips:

  1. Don't need to steam them. I don't even flour them. I just bake or deep fry after stuffing.

  2. Use ground turkey or pork instead of "minced." Skip the food pro. Just sauté garlic and onion a few minutes in olive oil, add ground pork and seasoning. Reserve. This recipe doesn't list bean thread noodles, but you will need those obviously. About 7 oz bean thread (super thin rice noodle/glass noodle) will do. Cook those then stir fry them in with the meat mixture. Adjust seasoning.

  3. Lime leaf can be hard to find, I don't usually use it. A little cilantro and a squeeze of lime juice can help balance the fish sauce. A bit of fresh grated ginger is also nice.

  4. Go slow on adding fish sauce!!! Every brand is a bit different and the amount is very dependent on personal taste. I start with 1/2 tsp! I also season with a little hosing and maybe a dash of soy sauce.

  5. A knife like this is best for deboning the wings. It takes practice to debone them without splitting the skin. Also plan about 2-3 hours for 14 wings (unless you are an old Southeast Asian woman that has done this her whole life). Start by cutting and pushing the meat down from the shoulder joint end of the wing. Turn it inside out and pull it down to the elbow joint. Scrape around until you see the tendon and ligaments, then cut those (they look like strings) and push down the meat until you can pull it again. At the wrist joint above the wing tip, crack the bones and remove them (I save mine in the freezer for chicken stock). Then invert the wing and you will have a deboned chicken wing!
